jobs.description:
Job Overview

This post is fixed term/secondment until 28 February 2027 to meet the service needs  

If you are interested in applying for the secondment position, you must obtain permission from your current line manager prior to applying for this post.

We are pleased to advertise an exciting secondment opportunity for a Senior Workforce Planning Officer within the People Services Team. This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop expertise in workforce planning while working with colleagues across BCUHB to support the delivery of robust workforce plans and sustainable workforce solutions.

Main duties of the job

Support workforce planning and education commissioning projects across BCUHB, working with services to develop workforce plans, analyse workforce data, identify future workforce needs, to help services deliver sustainable workforce solutions. You’ll engage with a wide range of stakeholders, provide workforce planning advice and training, and contribute to service improvement and workforce redesign initiatives.

The role requires resilience and professionalism, a proactive and analytical individual with experience in workforce planning, project management, service improvement or transformation. You’ll have strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, be confident working with data and producing reports and undertaking training.

We are looking for someone who can motivate and build relationships across services, work independently and maintain momentum when managing competing priorities.

Working for our organisation

If you relish a challenge, have a passion to help others or simply fancy a fresh start, then Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) North Wales, has all the right ingredients. The largest health organisation in Wales, providing a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and elective hospital services for a population of around 700,000, across North Wales . Join our team and get the support you need, in line with our Organisational Values and ‘Proud to Lead’ competence framework.

Enjoy being part of working with engaged leadership at all levels, and be assured we are committed to promoting equality and diversity, and are proud to welcome applicants under the “Disability Confident Employer” scheme.

Please check your email account regularly. Successful applicants will receive all recruitment related correspondence via the email account registered on the application form.

Applications may be submitted in Welsh. Applications submitted in Welsh will not be treated less favourably than an application submitted in English.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

Support the organisation to plan their workforce by using standardised approaches and methodology to deliver robust workforce plans.
Support the development of local workforce plans aligned to the BCU workforce planning process, and work with stakeholders to embed within the service and financial planning cycle.
Promote workforce models which support multi-disciplinary, multi-professional and multi-agency workforce plans across services, supporting discussions to drive changes to skill mix including the use of extended, advanced and new roles to foster innovation and workforce redesign, considering patient pathways, providing support and guidance in the delivery of workforce solutions appropriate to the needs of the service.
Delivering data improvement work including data entry, cleansing and data quality improvement, analytics and dashboard reporting
Ensure that workforce planning monitoring reports are accurate and informative, accompanied by adequate explanation and presented in a manner which is easily understandable for the target audience and related to organisational needs; working with finance colleagues and others to ensure consistency of data reported.
Act as a workforce planning expert in the use of workforce planning tools.
Deliver workforce planning engagement sessions, training and advice and guidance on resources within the organisation.
Taking an active role in the workforce planning meetings and events to support them in their role.

Person specification

Qualifications And Knowledge

Essential criteria

Educated to Degree level or possess equivalent experience/qualifications or significant experience of working at a similar level in a specialist area ie: Workforce Planning, Workforce Optimisation/Transformation.
Project management specialist knowledge acquired through post graduate diploma level or relevant demonstrable equivalent experience acquired in a specialist HR setting.
Understanding of programme/project management processes
Demonstration of Continued Professional Development (CPD).
Knowledge of NHS/BCU organisation policies, processes and culture.
A willingness to undertake training as appropriate to the role.

Desirable criteria

Knowledge and understanding of The Six Steps Methodology to Integrated Workforce Planning.
Demonstrate knowledge of new and emerging initiatives in Workforce Planning

Experience

Essential criteria

Experience in delivery of workforce planning.
Demonstrable project management experience with evidence of affecting change, process redesign and establishing monitoring/evaluation mechanisms ideally within an NHS setting.
Experience of working in partnership with a range of organisations and stakeholders.
Experience of working to targets and outcomes in a programme management environment.
Experience of developing a range of reports displaying analysis and supporting narrative pieces in relation to complex information and writing concise and effective reports.
Experience of producing project plans, risk logs, issues logs, milestones, needs assessments, training and communication plans.
Experience of developing and delivering training and presentations.
Experience of service improvements/optimisation and development.

Desirable criteria

Experience of undertaking strategic workforce planning.
Experience of working within the NHS.

Skills And Attributes

Essential criteria

Welsh Language Skills are desirable levels 1 to 3 in understanding, speaking, reading, and writing in Welsh or willingness to work towards achieving this at levels 1-3.
Ability to develop and maintain effective working partnerships with operational staff, professional groups and senior managers within the organisation and other relevant internal or external stakeholders.
Ability to receive and communicate complex information in a multi-disciplinary working environment and across organisations
Demonstrable experience of planning over short, medium and long-term timeframes and adjustment of plans and resource requirements accordingly.
Good analytical skills with the ability to analyse and interpret complex information from a wide range of sources and produce high quality written reports in an appropriate format for the target audience.
Able to interpret national, regional and local priorities and support services understanding objectives in line with such priority agendas.
Able to work autonomously, effectively and efficiently under pressure.
IT Skills: word processing, PowerPoint, spreadsheets, BI dashboards, ESR, O365 products and SharePoint.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager - Sustainability
jobs.description:
Customer Success Manager (UK)

Job description

Tracera (Formerly ESG Flo) is seeking a dedicated Customer Success Manager to join our team. In this role, you'll collaborate closely with our Sales and Product teams to ensure successful delivery for our clients, drive long-term retention, and act as the bridge between client feedback and Product teams. You will also serve as a trusted Tracera expert, helping clients get lasting value from the platform. We’re excited to announce an opportunity to join our growing European Customer Success team, reporting directly to Customer Success leadership. This role offers a unique chance to help shape our customer success strategies across Europe and make a significant impact on the company.

Our goal is to make ESG data collection and reporting easy, efficient, and enjoyable. We help sustainability teams focus on driving meaningful impact in Environmental, Social, and Governance domains rather than getting bogged down with reporting tasks.

How did Tracera come about?
Tracera is an AI-enabled Data management and reporting solution designed to automate the ESG data gathering process and provide real-time insights into ESG factors. This software makes ESG reporting and decision making seamless by optimizing extraction, validation, and transformation of relevant data. It is built from the ground up with auditability in mind.

Tracera aligns operations with global climate goals, promotes social responsibility, and enhances corporate governance practices. Their 5 values are: Truth, Trust, Transparency, Totality and Time.

Tracera was founded in 2022 and is headquartered in New York. Tracera receives funding and support from Bain & Company as well as other top VCs.

What will I be doing?
In this role, you will play a crucial part in guiding our clients through their sustainability journeys. You will act as a dedicated point of contact for a portfolio of existing clients, ensuring successful delivery and long-term retention by understanding their pain points, addressing questions, assisting with training, and identifying areas for improvement on an ongoing basis. The majority of your time (around 70%) will be spent on ad hoc Scope 3 consulting, supporting customers beyond the Tracera platform with work such as mapping emissions across the 15 Scope 3 categories, cleaning and standardizing supplier data, and improving calculation methodologies. You will also support new clients as they get started on the platform and have opportunities to collaborate with the Product team by sharing client feedback and helping to prioritize new features.

To be more specific, you will engage in the following tasks:

Client Account Management

Prepare and lead regular check-ins with existing clients to understand their processes, evolving data challenges, and how Tracera can continue to support them.
Build a deep understanding of each customer’s profile and organizational structure, including key stakeholders, decision-makers, reporting lines, and how sustainability and data responsibilities are distributed across their teams.
Drive ongoing adoption of Tracera’s Scopes 1, 2, 3, and Compliance Reporting Platforms, including data organization and follow-ups, AI/ML engagement, and continued support, while also guiding new clients through onboarding as needed.
Partner with existing clients to identify expansion and mutual growth opportunities as their needs evolve.
Conduct training sessions and workshops for client teams on an ongoing basis, including onboarding new users as client teams and responsibilities change.
Work closely with client Sustainability Teams and gain valuable exposure to ESG topics.

Collaboration with Customer Success Team

Work directly with Customer Success leadership on account management to ensure successful client relationships.
Partner with fellow customer success data analysts to streamline client onboarding and data organization.
Ensure the team meets all deadlines for client onboarding.
Maintain the highest standards of transparency & accuracy throughout the onboarding process.
Engage with internal and external auditors on Tracera’s platforms with clients.

Collaboration with Product and Engineering Teams

Provide customer feedback to the Product team, help prioritize features, and act as a liaison between clients and the Product team.
Report bugs and issues to the engineering team for resolution.
Manage customer bug tickets and provide updates to clients based on communication from the engineering team.

Ad Hoc Consulting & Scope 3 Data Cleaning

Deliver ad hoc consulting engagements for clients, from scoping requests and setting timelines to delivering results that extend beyond the Tracera platform, including projects such as water footprint analysis and target tracking.
Lead Scope 3 data cleaning projects, reviewing, standardizing, and categorizing client spend, activity, and supplier data so it maps accurately to the relevant Scope 3 categories.
Using Excel and other data analysis tools, identify gaps, errors, and inconsistencies in client Scope 3 datasets, and flag critical changes to historical data or current calculations that could affect reported figures.
Assist clients with related analyses, such as calculating carbon footprints across Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions.

That sounds just right to me. Who are we looking for?

Qualifications
You have experience in excel, data organization, and project management
You have had client facing roles
A background in carbon accounting, including hands-on experience building GHG inventories and calculating Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions in line with the GHG Protocol
Deep expertise in Scope 3 specifically: you understand all 15 categories, can work with spend-based, activity-based, and supplier-specific methods, and know how to help clients tackle supplier data collection and data quality challenges
Undergraduate or graduate degrees in environmental science or sustainability, or experience in a similar role/industry is a plus
Bonus points for familiarity with the software startup ecosystem
Bonus points for speaking another language (German, Italian, Dutch)

Qualities
You thrive within a high-speed startup
You are a thought leader who is comfortable engaging with clients daily and providing recommendations on projects at hand
You are a hands-on problem solver, proactively approaching challenges with a positive attitude.
You are an empathetic team player willing to jump in and do whatever it takes

Please note that this role begins with a 90-day evaluation period during which you will collaborate with the team to define your objectives. Your performance will be assessed based on these objectives at the end of the 90-day window.

Why should I join Tracera?
You will be joining an exciting seed stage startup with a clear mission to simplify ESG compliance. We are a group of smart, hard-working, passionate, and fun-loving individuals committed to making the world a better place. Here, you can leave your mark by supporting our clients on their most pressing issues.

To apply, please submit both a resume and cover letter to hr@tracera.com. Be sure to showcase your experience working with clients and/or on various projects. Any sustainability background is a plus! Additionally, please provide details of your role on the projects you've been involved in.

jobs.description:
We're hiring a Customer Success Engineer to help customers turn our product into part of their everyday work. You'll combine practical customer success with building the systems, communications and learning experiences that make adoption repeatable.

About Us

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

Our values are Own It, Ship It and Don't Be Boring
. We move quickly, challenge each other kindly and care about making something customers actually use.

The Challenge

A useful product does not automatically become a useful daily habit. Customers need to connect their data, complete a valuable piece of work and come back to do it again. Your job is to make those steps easier, then make them work consistently across customers.

Imagine several customers are getting stuck connecting Microsoft 365. You help one through the setup, identify the shared problem, improve the guidance and follow-ups, and check whether more people reach their first useful result.

About You

You like helping people and making things. When the same question comes up twice, you start thinking about a better way to answer it. You can learn a technical product, explain it clearly and follow a problem through without waiting for a perfect brief.

You've probably spent one to three years in a technical customer role, implementation, support or operations. Strong projects, internships or your own business can demonstrate the same ability.

Your Impact

A practical individual contributor role, working directly with our CTO and closely with Customer Success, Account Management, Product and Engineering.
A builder who learns from individual customer problems and creates solutions that help many customers.
Ownership of onboarding, adoption programs and routine-support improvements, with experienced colleagues to learn from.

What This Role Is Not

A sales-quota or renewals role. Account Management owns commercial relationships.
A role spent solely answering tickets. You need time to build the systems that reduce repeat questions.
A senior software-engineering or bespoke enterprise-implementation role.

Day to Day, You Will

Build adoption programs: onboarding sequences, useful prompts and follow-ups based on what customers have actually done.
Improve first-line support: handle questions, find recurring issues, maintain useful guidance and build AI-assisted answers and routing, with tested output and clear human escalation.
Teach customers: run onboarding, webinars and office hours; make short videos, examples and guides people can use independently.
Make product releases useful: explain what changed, reach the people who will benefit and check whether they use it.
Troubleshoot: investigate configuration and integration issues, fix what you can and give engineers clear reproductions when the product needs to change.
Measure progress: track time to first value, repeat use and the manual work removed. Use the evidence to decide what to improve next.

What We're Looking For

Something useful you built yourself: an automation, small tool or integration you can explain and improve.
Practical AI use, with a habit of testing answers and checking what your tools produce.
Clear writing, patient teaching and confidence working directly with customers.
Comfort connecting tools and data through APIs, webhooks, scripting or automation platforms.
Reliable follow-through and enough data confidence to tell whether your work helped.

Nice To Have (But Not Required)

Experience with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, product analytics, SQL or lifecycle communications.
Experience running training or supporting a specialist professional product.
Real estate or investment-management knowledge. You can learn the domain here.

Your First Few Months

Month 1. You can lead an onboarding session, have investigated real customer questions and have shipped your first useful automation or adoption improvement.
Month 3. A repeatable onboarding or feature-adoption program is running. You can show customers reaching value faster, using a valuable process more consistently, or the team doing less repetitive work.
Month 6. The programs you own reliably serve more customers without a matching rise in manual effort. You can explain which interventions improve sustained use and which you stopped. You and Chen will set targets from the starting baseline.

What We Offer You

Salary: £50,000–£70,000, plus equity. Hybrid, 2-3 days a week in the office.

Enhanced pension contributions and private healthcare through BUPA.
Generous paid time off and a two-week company shutdown in December.
Enhanced parental leave: 14 weeks for the primary caregiver and six for the secondary caregiver.
Direct access to experienced technical and customer colleagues, with meaningful ownership from the start.

jobs.title: Customer Success Lead
jobs.description:
💬 Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage
to manage patient demand, and Self-Book
, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires
for long-term conditions, while Accumail
finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe
, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

That sounds cool - what does a Customer Success Lead have to do with it?

Accurx works with 41 of the 42 NHS ICBs and is growing fast in secondary care. To keep up with how the NHS is organising itself, our Account Management team has just moved to a regional model, with leads for London, the South and the North. The goal is simple: join up what we’re learning across primary care, secondary care, acute, community and mental health, and make sure the best opportunities get surfaced across the whole of England, not just in one set of ICBs.

We’re hiring a Customer Success Lead for the North. You’ll lead a team of Customer Success Managers across primary and secondary care and be the strategic, zoomed-out view of the region. Your team is close to the accounts. Your job is to spot the patterns across them, turn what they’re hearing into strategy, and help Accurx show up at a regional level.

The challenges you’ll solve as a Customer Success Lead

Lead and grow a team of CSMs. You’ll start with three CSMs, each with their own region, customers and stage of the customer journey. You’ll coach them, unblock them and help them do the best work of their careers.
Bring two very different care settings together. Primary care is about deepening trust we’ve built over years. Secondary care is about firsts: new services, longer implementations and goalposts that move. You’ll work out what connects them, what doesn’t, and where learnings from one can speed up the other.
Turn insight into strategy. Your team will feed you what’s happening on the ground. You’ll spot trends, gaps and duplicated effort across the region and turn them into projects, goals and growth opportunities in products like Accurx Scribe and Total Triage.
Own the commercial picture for your region. You’ll keep a close eye on churn, risk, renewals and upsell across your team’s accounts, and represent the region at our weekly business reviews with the exec team.
Build the playbook with your fellow leads. The regional model is brand new. Alongside the leads for London and the South, you’ll shape how we work, what best practice looks like and how we scale it.
Be the link across the business. You’ll work closely with implementation, transformation, support and business development, making sure the voice of our customers shapes where Accurx goes next.

You should apply if...

You’ve led customer-facing teams. You have a few years of people management in customer success or account management, and you love helping others grow.
You’ve built things from the ground up. You’ve been on a startup to scale-up journey, worn a lot of hats, and taken customers from never having heard of you to being your biggest advocates.
You care about depth, not volume. You’ve looked after long-standing, strategic relationships rather than a high-volume queue, and you know that trust is what makes customers stick.
You can zoom out. You don’t need to be in the weeds of every account. You’re great at spotting patterns, asking the right questions and knowing where your team needs you most.
You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You’re happy to try something, get it wrong, learn and go again. Process is something you create, not something you wait for.
You’re a big collaborator. You’re an incredible communicator and listener, and you know the best outcomes come from working across teams.
You’re curious about the NHS. Healthcare experience is welcome but not essential. What matters is empathy for the pressure the NHS is under and the patience to build trust in a complex system.

What’s in it for me?

You’ll be joining an established but fast-growing Tech for Good movement, where we’re led by our Principles and our mission to Solve Healthcare Productivity.

£70,000 - £90,000 salary + share options up to £30,000
Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life
Flexible Working: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office 3 days a week, with core hours of 10am-4pm
Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year
Family matters: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support
We have our very own Chef! Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches will be provided, with the occasional sweet treat!

Want to know more about the company or the hiring process? Check out our Careers page and Candidate hub.

Find us across social media: Medium, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and YouTube.

Diversity and Equal Opportunities:
We are an equal opportunities employer and a pleasant and supportive place to work. We particularly welcome applications from those who are significantly underrepresented in the technology sector, such as women, non-binary people, transgender people, people with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ community and individuals from Black and Minority Ethnic communities.

Compliance Analyst I, II or III

Hybrid role (3 days/week in office) at our Portland, Medford, Fargo, Burlington, Vancouver, Renton, Boise, Lewiston or Salt Lake City offices. Candidates must reside within commutable distance of that location.

Build a career with purpose. Join our
Cause
to create a person-focused and economically sustainable health care system.

Who We Are Looking For

Every day, Cambia’s dedicated team of Compliance Analysts is living our mission to make health care easier and lives better. As a member of the Compliance team, our Compliance Analysts responsible to deliver an effective compliance program. They design, implement, deliver, measure and refine activities and controls to prevent, detect and correct violations of state, federal and other laws. Duties may include, but are not limited to, risk assessment, training, monitoring, auditing, regulatory audit, and market conduct activities, audit coordination, investigation, root cause analysis, regulatory implementation, control assessment, reporting, and corrective actions – all in service of creating a person-focused health care experience.

Do you have a passion for serving others and learning new things? Do you thrive as part of a collaborative, caring team? Then this role may be the perfect fit.

Qualifications

What You Bring to Cambia:

Compliance Specialist I would have a Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience and 3 years of experience in a role demonstrating success in compliance-related activities and controls (e.g, risk assessments, training, monitoring, auditing, investigations, root causes analysis, control assessments reporting or corrective actions) with experience in a health care or Medicare-regulated environment preferred.

Compliance Specialist II would have a Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; 5 years of compliance experience or equivalent related experience, with experience in a health care or Medicare-regulated environment preferred.

Compliance Specialist III would have at least a Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; 8 years of compliance experience or equivalent related experience, with experience in a health care or Medicare-regulated environment or ACA-regulated environment preferred.

Skills And Attributes

Proven ability to deliver effective Core Compliance activities, including, monitoring, auditing, root cause analyses, and corrective actions.
Skilled in project management and delivery including proven ability to initiate and manage multiple projects and priorities.
Excellent written and oral communication and presentation skills.
Excellent research and analytics skills, with proven ability to distill actionable, practical advice from diverse sources and opinions. Legal research skills preferred.
Proven ability to influence effectively at all levels of the organization.
Excellent independent judgment and decision-making skills.
PC literate with office computer software - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Visio, etc.
Discretion and confidentiality.
Agile, with high learning velocity.
Experience with AI tools and technologies to enhance productivity and decision-making in professional settings highly desired

Additional Skills And Attributes For Compliance Analyst II

Demonstrated fluency in organizational agility: knowledgeable how about organizations work and how to get things done through formal and informal channels.
Practical familiarity with legal requirements relating to assigned compliance program, or for new hires, practical familiarity with analogous legal requirements.
Demonstrated mastery of at least four Compliance functions , to include the core competencies: risk assessments, training, policies and procedures, monitoring, auditing, external audit coordination, control assessments, reporting, corrective actions, implementation oversight, and ability to perform those compliance functions effectively within that compliance program; or if assigned to a specialized function (e.g. FDR/ DDE Compliance, Marketing Materials Review, Data Validations), mastery of all competencies related to that specialized function.
Demonstrated ability to handle successfully at least medium-complexity, medium-difficulty matters end-to-end.
Demonstrated ability to drive success with challenging partners.

Additional Skills And Attributes For Compliance Analyst III

Demonstrated mastery of legal requirements relating to assigned compliance program; or for new hires, demonstrated mastery of analogous legal requirements.
Demonstrated mastery of at least 6 core compliance functions, including the core competencies and ability to deftly perform all compliance functions relating to assigned compliance program as needed.
Demonstrated ability to handle successfully the most complex, most difficult matters end-to-end.
Demonstrated ability to drive success with the most challenging and/or most elevated partners.
Demonstrated excellence in building effective relationships at all levels of the organization; influencing decision-making; effectively framing issues and dialogues; and driving successful outcomes.
Demonstrated, end-to-end operational knowledge relating to assigned compliance program.
Demonstrated peer mentoring and departmental leadership.
Experience with AI tools and technologies to enhance productivity and decision-making in professional settings highly desired

What You Will Do At Cambia

Overall responsibilities include specific and/or portions of the following functions that relate to an effective compliance program utilizing as a basis the seven elements of compliance.
Duties include aspects of the preparation, planning, coordination, project management, submission, administration, monitoring and auditing of the Cambia compliance program which serves to oversee activities related to requirements, laws and regulations to prevent, detect and remediate compliance issues of the company.
Responsibility for producing and maintaining policies and desk manuals for position.
Works as a team with other staff members assigned in either a supporting or leading role.
Participating in the annual risk assessment process.
Ensuring materials, reports, and other documents are written in an understandable and and concise style.
Project management and implementation.
Participating, supporting and serving in regular meetings, including divisional and cross-divisional committees as needed.
Core Competencies: risk assessments, training, policies and procedures, training, monitoring, auditing, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
Additional Competencies: external audit coordination, implementations, control assessments, delegation oversight, data validation, marketing material oversight, DDE/FDR oversight.

Work Environment

Travel rarely required, locally or out of state.
May be required to work outside normal hours.

Compliance Analyst I

Compliance Analyst III

Oregon, Washington, Utah, and Idaho: The expected hiring range is $101,200.00 – $136,900.00, the full salary range is $95,000.00 – $155,000.00 and the bonus target is 15%.
North Dakota: The expected hiring range is $90,906.79 - $122,991.55, the full salary range is $80,716.23 - $133,182.10.

About Cambia

Working at Cambia means being part of a purpose-driven, award-winning culture built on trust and innovation anchored in our 100+ year history. Our caring and supportive colleagues are some of the best and brightest in the industry, innovating together toward sustainable, person-focused health care. Whether we're helping members, lending a hand to a colleague or volunteering in our communities, our compassion, empathy and team spirit always shine through.

Why Join the Cambia Team?

At Cambia, You Can

Work alongside diverse teams building cutting-edge solutions to transform health care.
Earn a competitive salary and enjoy generous benefits while doing work that changes lives.
Grow your career with a company committed to helping you succeed.
Give back to your community by participating in Cambia-supported outreach programs.
Connect with colleagues who share similar interests and backgrounds through our employee resource groups.

We believe a career at Cambia is more than just a paycheck – and your compensation should be too. Our compensation package includes competitive base pay as well as a market-leading 401(k) with a significant company match, bonus opportunities and more.

Benefits

In exchange for helping members live healthy lives, we offer benefits that empower you to do the same. Just a few highlights include:

Medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and their eligible family members, including mental health benefits.
Annual employer contribution to a health savings account.
Generous paid time off varying by role and tenure in addition to 10 company-paid holidays.
Market-leading retirement plan including a company match on employee 401(k) contributions, with a potential discretionary contribution based on company performance (no vesting period).
Up to 12 weeks of paid parental time off (eligibility requires 12 months of continuous service with Cambia immediately preceding leave).
Award-winning wellness programs that reward you for participation.
Employee Assistance Fund for those in need.
Commute and parking benefits.

Learn More About Our Benefits.

We are happy to offer work from home options for most of our roles. To take advantage of this flexible option, we require employees to have a wired internet connection that is not satellite or cellular and internet service with a minimum upload speed of 5Mb and a minimum download speed of 10 Mb.

As part of our security requirements, new hires will need access to a personal mobile device to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) upon joining the company. MFA is an important layer of protection for accessing Cambia systems and is required for all employees.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other status protected by law. new_jobs.title: Information Technology Risk & Compliance Analyst
new_jobs.description:
ECMC Group is a nonprofit corporation focused on helping students succeed. Headquartered in Minneapolis, ECMC Group and its family of companies provide financial tools and services, as well as funding for innovative programs to help students achieve their academic and professional goals.

Job Summary

Responsible for planning, executing and reporting on complex IT compliance activities and related initiatives across information systems. Performs assigned portions of IT compliance programs, determining compliance with policies and procedures, monitoring, recommending corrective action, preparing findings, and assisting with remediation plans. Reviews and services should be performed in accordance with professional and department standards.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Leads and performs complex IT compliance activities including planning, risk analysis, testing and reporting in accordance with professional and department standards.
Leads vendor security risk assessments and reviews security and compliance provisions within vendor contracts in partnership with procurement and legal teams.
Independently engages management to assess processes, identify control weaknesses and discuss compliance observations and risks.
Secures management ownership of findings and remediation plans and monitors remediation progress through completion.
Prepares clear documentation and draft reports communicating results, risks and recommendations to improve information system controls and practices.
Plans and executes IT compliance reviews and supports internal and external audits through evidence preparation and auditor coordination.
Contributes to enterprise risk assessments by identifying emerging risks, control gaps and improvement opportunities.
Provides guidance and informal coaching to staff on compliance activities of low to medium complexity as assigned.
Anticipates and manages stakeholder expectations while ensuring timely, consistent delivery of compliance services.
Communicates complex compliance concepts clearly to peers, leaders and business partners.
Performs other duties or responsibilities as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in computer information systems, information technology, legal studies, or related field or an additional 2 years of relevant experience in lieu of degree.
Understanding of IT concepts such as identity and access management, threat and vulnerability management, data loss prevention, change management, data analytics, and software development lifecycle
3+ years of experience in IT risk and compliance, IT governance, IT auditing or an IT related field
Experience assessing vendor risk, performing security assessments, and reviewing contracts
Experience working with procurement and legal teams
Experience assessing security controls for AWS or cloud environments
Experience developing and maintaining policies and/or information management frameworks
Experience creating and assembling evidence for internal or external auditors
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office suite, including experience analyzing data using Excel and designing or managing SharePoint sites
General knowledge of security control concepts, principles, risk analysis, FISMA, PCI Compliance, HIPAA, Privacy, process improvement and techniques, including frameworks such as NIST, ISO2700, COSO and COBIT

Preferred Qualifications:

Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) certifications preferred

The pay range for this position is $90,000-$100,000. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as relevant experience, peer and market benchmarks, and geographic location.

This position is classified as hybrid
Monday - Wednesday and requires attendance in Minneapolis, MN
.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

ECMC Group also provides a comprehensive benefits package:

Health & wellness benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance plan options, with a generous employer subsidy. Company paid life & disability insurance, pre-tax flexible spending accounts and robust wellness programs.
Financial benefits: Generous 401(k) plan with a company match up to 6% and additional discretionary contribution potential, holiday time off, paid time off accrual starting at 20 days/year and commuter subsidy.
Education benefits: Tuition reimbursement up to $10,500/year for approved programs and student loan payment reimbursement up to $4,800/year. Up to $5,250 of qualifying education benefits can be reimbursed pre-tax.

Experience identifying compliance risks and recommending process or control improvements

new_jobs.title: Investment Compliance Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Weiss Asset Management (WAM), a Boston-based investment firm, is seeking an Investment Compliance Analyst to join our Compliance team. This role sits at the intersection of investment compliance, trading, and data, with responsibility for monitoring trade activity, resolving compliance exceptions, and improving the systems and processes that support ongoing compliance monitoring.

Candidates graduating in Summer 2027, as well as those with 1-3 years of relevant professional experience, are encouraged to apply. Working proficiency in SQL is required; experience with Python, automation, AI tools, or order management systems is a plus. This is a full-time, in-office role based in Boston.

Responsibilities:

Monitor and resolve pre- and post-trade compliance alerts across funds and strategies, using data to spot exceptions and patterns and escalating issues with traders and internal teams as needed.
Interpret, maintain, and test trading compliance rules in the firm's order management system (OMS), and support investment-related compliance questions.
Analyze trade, position, and compliance data in SQL to support recurring reviews, reconciliations, and investigations.
Automate manual tasks with code and AI tools, building solutions that make compliance monitoring more efficient and repeatable.
Design systematic, scalable workflows for compliance reviews and escalations.
Maintain restricted securities and issuer lists across firm systems and support wall-crossing and MNPI processes.
Track regulatory developments and assess their impact on trading activity, compliance rules, policies, and procedures.
Support regulatory filings, audits, system upgrades, and ad-hoc compliance projects.

Base Salary:
$85,000–$125,000 per year, depending on experience. Actual compensation will reflect the candidate's skills, relevant experience, and overall fit for the role. It is unlikely that all new hires will start at the top of this range.

About the Company:

For 34 years, Weiss Asset Management has developed proprietary investment strategies designed to deliver high risk-adjusted returns to our investors, who include charitable foundations, pension plans, endowments, hospitals, government entities and private investors. We manage approximately $4.5 billion across our hedge fund clients. We work collaboratively to solve problems, and to identify undervalued assets through deep fundamental research, statistical analysis and an analytically rigorous approach to decision making. Above all else, we value integrity, uncompromising rationality, creativity and entrepreneurship, and continuous learning and improvement.

Our team of over 140 individuals is the engine of our success, and we welcome truly exceptional candidates from all backgrounds.

WAM is a fit for you if :
You enjoy a collaborative environment, where decisions are made in diverse teams. At WAM, all employees can expect to work directly with members of other departments representing a range of backgrounds.
You work well in a flat structure and are comfortable voicing dissenting opinion. Talent and work ethic will dictate what you can achieve at WAM, as evidenced by the fact that our president and the majority of our managing directors began their careers here as interns.
You are driven to constantly learn, improve, and make rational decisions based in fact and data, and you welcome receiving feedback as well as sharing knowledge with others.
You prioritize acting ethically in all situations.

WAM is an equal opportunity employer. Women, minorities, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply.
